findings.bible: Buffer updates and instancing: update options still have meaning on EasyGL, SDL GPU, D3D9 and D3D11 (discard/no-overwrite map to distinct native operations); Vulkan inherits the option-discarding default; WebGPU, D3D12, Software and Headless override it without preserving option identity.
findings.target: modules/renderers/directx12/src/D3D12Buffers.cpp::D3D12VertexBufferRenderer::UploadAndCopy (a switch over None/Discard/NoOverwrite that does the same for all three); modules/renderers/software/src/SoftwareRenderer.cpp::SoftwareVertexBufferRenderer::SetDataWithOptions and modules/renderers/headless/src/HeadlessRenderer.cpp::HeadlessVertexBufferRenderer::SetDataWithOptions (both call SetData and ignore the option); modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp::WebGPUVertexBufferRenderer::SetDataWithOptions (WEBGPU-44 comment: deliberately not branched on). By contrast D3D9 D3D9Buffers.cpp::LockFlagsFor, D3D11 D3D11Buffers.cpp::MapTypeFor, EasyGL EasyGLVertexBufferRenderer::uploadWithOptions, OpenGL4 OpenGL4VertexBufferRenderer::Upload, SDL_GPU SdlGpuVertexBufferRenderer::SetDataWithOptions (cycle = options != NoOverwrite) and FNA3D Fna3dResources.cpp::ResolveSetDataOptions do map the option to a different native operation.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/renderers/renderer-contract.html#default-kinds: lists ten overriding families and says only 'Vulkan inherits the option-dropping default, and WebGPU's override also ignores the option', which implies every other overrider honours Discard/NoOverwrite. The DirectX 12, Software and Headless overrides do not.

fix.old_html: SetDataWithOptions is overridden by DirectX 9, DirectX 11, DirectX 12, EasyGL, FNA3D, Headless, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, Software and WebGPU; Vulkan inherits the option-dropping default, and WebGPU's override also ignores the option.
fix.html: SetDataWithOptions is overridden by DirectX 9, DirectX 11, DirectX 12, EasyGL, FNA3D, Headless, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, Software and WebGPU, but an override does not mean the hint is honoured. Only DirectX 9 (D3DLOCK_DISCARD versus D3DLOCK_NOOVERWRITE), DirectX 11 (D3D11_MAP_WRITE_DISCARD versus D3D11_MAP_WRITE_NO_OVERWRITE), EasyGL and OpenGL4 (orphan the buffer store versus write into it), SDL_GPU (cycle the buffer unless the option is NoOverwrite) and FNA3D (its own set-data option, degraded to None where the driver cannot guarantee no-overwrite) turn Discard and NoOverwrite into different native operations. Vulkan inherits the option-dropping default, and the WebGPU, DirectX 12, Software and Headless overrides treat all three options identically (WebGPU because every draw snapshots its bytes, DirectX 12 because its per-frame upload ring already covers both, Software and Headless by forwarding to plain SetData).

fix.old_html: Other gaps have no capability member at all: whether back-buffer readback exists, which image it returns, whether a clear is aspect-selective, whether viewport and scissor are rasterised. Those are covered on Presentation and back-buffer readback and Targets, clears and viewports.
fix.html:
Other gaps have no capability member at all: whether back-buffer readback exists, which image it returns, whether a clear is aspect-selective, whether viewport and scissor are rasterised. Those are covered on Presentation and back-buffer readback and Targets, clears and viewports.

The resource-side defaults for targets lean in opposite directions. IRenderTargetRenderer::GetMultiSampleCount() defaults to 0, which is conservative: no multisampling is claimed. HasRealDepthBuffer(requested) and the target's GetAppliedDepthStencilFormatEXT(requested) default to echoing the request, and HasRealStencilBuffer delegates to the depth answer, so a family that never allocates a depth plane can still appear to own the one the game asked for; only an override makes the answer truthful (the 2D-only SDL_RENDERER targets, for example, answer false). The device consults these answers to decide which clear aspects and discard planes exist, so the applied sample count and the real attachment presence are stronger facts than the constructor arguments.

findings.bible: Confirmed pre-existing gaps (default backbuffer): SDL/GL chooses framebuffer 0 after CNA asks for the selected GL profile and eight stencil bits; when back-buffer MSAA is active CNA replaces that path with its own RGBA8 plus depth renderbuffers; the requested enums are not what the default framebuffer uses.
findings.target: modules/renderers/easygl/src/EasyGLRenderer.cpp::RequestedGlContext (depthBits = 24, stencilBits = 8, doubleBuffer = true for every profile, independent of DepthFormat); EasyGLRenderer::BindDefaultFramebuffer (sampleCount_ <= 1 unbinds to framebuffer 0; only the MSAA branch rebuilds storage for backBufferDepthFormat_ via CreateMsaaBuffers); EasyGLRenderer::UpdatePresentationFormatEXT (stores backBufferDepthFormat_, ignores colour format and fullscreen); ApplyDepthStencilState (stencil test enabled only when bound_->depthFormat == 3).
findings.site_now: deep-dives/renderers/easygl-state-and-resource-semantics.html#default-backbuffer: describes only the MSAA framebuffer rebuilding for the selected DepthFormat and says the stencil test needs a plane the back buffer 'really has'; never says that without MSAA the back buffer is framebuffer 0 with a fixed 24/8 request, so DepthFormat None/Depth16 has no storage effect there.

fix.old_html: The stencil test is enabled only while the active target or back buffer really has a Depth24Stencil8 plane.
fix.html: Without multisampling the back buffer is the platform's own framebuffer 0, and its depth and stencil planes are fixed when the GL context is created: the family's context request (RequestedGlContext) asks for 24 depth bits, 8 stencil bits and double buffering whatever DepthFormat the game selected, so requesting None or Depth16 does not shrink or remove it. The requested format decides only which tests the renderer enables (the depth test needs a format other than None; the stencil test needs Depth24Stencil8, although the context request always asks for stencil bits) and how the renderbuffers of the multisample framebuffer are built when back-buffer MSAA replaces framebuffer 0. A render target's stencil test, by contrast, follows the plane that target really owns.

findings.bible: Confirmed pre-existing gaps: the bare DrawColoredPrimitives callbacks receive matrices but no GpuDrawParams by contract; EasyGL's effect-aware stock path is its separate Draw*PrimitivesEx route, so the colored callback alone is not evidence that a supplied effect payload was discarded.
findings.target: modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp::IGraphicsRenderer::DrawColoredPrimitives and DrawIndexedColoredPrimitives (parameters: buffers, world/view/projection, primitive, count; doc comment: 'applies a basic colored-vertex shader (equivalent to BasicEffect with VertexColorEnabled = true)'; both are pure virtual) versus DrawPrimitivesEx/DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx which take GpuDrawParams.
findings.site_now: absent: the ledger (WP08-ch22-016) cites deep-dives/renderers/renderer-contract.html#draw-routes, but that section only discusses the effect-aware defaults and never states that the bare coloured draws have no payload by contract.

fix.old_html: A test of a custom vertex layout must still check pixels or bindings, not only that the call returned.
fix.html:
A test of a custom vertex layout must still check pixels or bindings, not only that the call returned.

The bare coloured draws are a different contract from the effect-aware ones. DrawColoredPrimitives and DrawIndexedColoredPrimitives take only the buffers, the world, view and projection matrices, the primitive type and the count; the header describes the renderer as applying a basic coloured-vertex shader, equivalent to BasicEffect with VertexColorEnabled = true, and they carry no GpuDrawParams by design. A family whose coloured callback ignores an applied effect is therefore not, by that alone, discarding a payload it was given; the question for such a family is whether its Draw*PrimitivesEx route, which does receive the payload, reached the native stock or custom program.

findings.bible: Remaining limitation: the extreme-magnitude RasterizerState.DepthBias case produced no visible bias on Vulkan (and on D3D9), so the evidence does not attribute it to Vulkan rather than the driver environment.
findings.target: modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp::VulkanRenderer::ApplyRasterizerState stores depthBias_ and slopeScaleDepthBias_ raw, and the 3D replay issues vkCmdSetDepthBias(cb, draw.depthBias, 0.0f, draw.slopeScaleDepthBias) with no depth-format scaling (VulkanRenderer does not override DepthBufferBitsEXT). Contrast modules/renderers/opengl4/src/OpenGL4Renderer.cpp::ApplyCurrentDepthBias ('FNA exposes constant DepthBias in normalized depth units ... passing the XNA value through raw ... is indistinguishable from no bias at all'; scales 65,535 for Depth16 and 16,777,215 for Depth24/Depth24Stencil8, and EasyGLRenderer::ApplyCurrentDepthBias uses the same two values), modules/renderers/common/d3d/src/D3DStateMapping.cpp::XnaDepthBiasToD3D (65,535 / 16,777,215 and 8,388,607 for D32_FLOAT, 'FNA3D uses C's float-to-int conversion'), modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/src/SdlGpuRenderer.cpp::XnaToSdlDepthBiasScale (65,535 / 16,777,215 / 8,388,607, 'the same per-format conversion used by FNA3D's SDL_gpu driver') and WebGPURenderer.cpp (fixed 16,777,215 scale, citing FNA's XNAToGL_DepthBiasScale). The 8,388,607 entry is therefore an FNA3D SDL_gpu / CNA D3D and SDL_GPU detail, not part of FNA3D's OpenGL and D3D11 table.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/renderers/vulkan-deferred-state-and-descriptors.html#depth-bias: 'RasterizerState.DepthBias maps to vkCmdSetDepthBias's constant factor ... matching FNA's glPolygonOffset(slopeScaleDepthBias, depthBias)'. FNA does not pass the value through unscaled; the sentence hides the conversion gap and repeats a stale source comment.

fix.old_html: RasterizerState.DepthBias maps to vkCmdSetDepthBias's constant factor and SlopeScaleDepthBias to its slope factor, matching FNA's glPolygonOffset(slopeScaleDepthBias, depthBias).
fix.html: RasterizerState.DepthBias is handed to vkCmdSetDepthBias as its constant factor and SlopeScaleDepthBias as its slope factor, both unconverted. That is not what FNA3D does: it multiplies the normalised XNA DepthBias by a per-depth-format scale (65,535 for Depth16 and 16,777,215 for Depth24 and Depth24Stencil8; its SDL_gpu driver adds 8,388,607 for 32-bit float depth) before applying it, and CNA's EasyGL, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, WebGPU and Direct3D 11 and 12 renderers convert it as well, whereas Vulkan's constant factor counts smallest resolvable depth steps. On this renderer a realistic XNA magnitude (around 1e-4) is therefore effectively no bias, and only very large values such as the test's -1e6 have an effect; the source comment that says the mapping matches FNA omits the scale.

findings.bible: Remaining limitation: extreme-magnitude DepthBias produced no visible bias on Vulkan (unresolved). The ledger closes it as 'a test defect' (VULKAN-091), which is true for the z=0 near-plane premise but leaves the product behaviour unexamined.
findings.target: modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp::ApplyRasterizerState and the draw replay (vkCmdSetDepthBias(cb, draw.depthBias, 0.0f, draw.slopeScaleDepthBias)) pass XNA's normalised DepthBias to a constant factor measured in minimum-resolvable depth steps, so a realistic XNA value (about 1e-4) offsets depth by roughly 1e-4 of one step, i.e. nothing. modules/renderers/vulkan/examples/vulkan_depth_bias_test.cpp uses -1e6 and -2e3 on purpose ('bias magnitudes are deliberately large') and therefore cannot see the defect. EasyGL, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, WebGPU and Direct3D 11/12 all convert; Vulkan does not. The renderer contract itself says a conversion is needed: modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp::IRenderTargetRenderer::DepthBufferBitsEXT documents that an API whose bias is a multiple of the smallest resolvable depth step, naming 'Vulkan's depthBiasConstantFactor', needs the depth width to convert; the SDL_GPU, EasyGL and OpenGL4 target classes override it and no Vulkan class does.
findings.site_now: Only a one-line mention in docs/xna-compatibility.html ('not scaled to renderer depth units on every renderer ... recorded as open on DirectX 11, Vulkan and PortableGL'); no Known Issues entry. That line looks stale for DirectX 11 (D3DStateMapping.cpp::XnaDepthBiasToD3D scales it and DirectX11Renderer applies it), so the Vulkan gap is the one that matters.
